sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Cockroach Janta Party Protests in Delhi Demanding Top Election Official's Resignation
cards.content: The Cockroach Janta Party led by Abhijeet Dipke is protesting in India's capital Delhi demanding the resignation of the top election official Gyanesh Kumar. Dipke was arrested and released saying the party won't back down or be intimidated. The protest has been ongoing for two days with thousands of security personnel deployed and roads barricaded. Police have detained and released many protesters and the internet has been curtailed in central Delhi. The party wants electoral reforms and accuses Kumar of manipulating voters' lists to favor Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party.

cards.title: One killed, 11 injured in Riyadh airport strike
cards.content: One person has been killed and 11 others injured in a second strike on the international airport in Riyadh Saudi Arabia. A projectile hit King Khalid International Airport causing a fire in a passenger hall. The Houthis in Yemen claimed responsibility and warned airlines and passengers not to use Saudi Arabian airports and airspace.

cards.title: Sudan: At Least 72 Civilians Killed in Air Strikes on Gold Miners
cards.content: At least 72 civilians who were searching for gold in Sudan's River Nile state were killed in air strikes on Saturday according to a regional rights group called Emergency Lawyers. The group says jets targeted the miners who were not armed and that the attack violates international humanitarian law and the right to life. The Sudanese government has not commented but Egypt has faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors in the past. The group believes the attack may be a war crime.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: US Job Postings for Software Developers Increase Despite AI Fears
cards.content: The number of job postings for software developers in the US has increased since February 2025 even as overall job postings decreased. This is surprising as many thought AI would replace the need for software developers. Instead companies are producing more code than ever before and software developers who work with AI are in high demand. The increase is concentrated in senior-level roles and positions that involve AI which has led some to believe that the profession is evolving rather than disappearing.

cards.title: AI Firms Partner with Nonprofits to Safeguard Advanced Models
cards.content: Independent evaluators mostly small nonprofits and accounting firms are being asked by AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI to help safeguard their advanced models and grow their businesses. This comes after a debate over whether they can safely develop and use their technology. Anthropic has pledged to embed independent evaluators in its company while OpenAI has already done so. However questions remain about how these third-party evaluators will be funded what level of access they will have and what the reporting structure will look like. Some experts say that without federal regulation the evaluators may be beholden to the AI companies for revenue which could lead to rubber-stamping of their findings.

cards.title: Fast-food Chains, Supermarkets Use AI for Dynamic Pricing, Personalization
cards.content: Fast-food chains and supermarkets are using artificial intelligence to set prices and personalize customer experiences. McDonald's is accused of using AI to charge different customers different prices for the same menu items. Grocery stores like Kroger are using AI to mark down near-expired food and supermarkets are using digital labels to display prices. Some companies are even using facial recognition to allow customers to pay with just a glance. Experts warn that this could lead to more dynamic pricing which means prices changing rapidly in response to changing market conditions. This could make it harder for consumers to compare prices and understand why they're paying certain prices.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: UK cancer deaths in children rise: parents urged to recognize clusters of symptoms
cards.content: Cancer is the leading cause of death from disease among children under 15 in the UK. Despite this many parents don't recognize the symptoms. For example 13-year-old Amelia Carroll was diagnosed with leukemia after her mother noticed bruises and tiredness. These symptoms were initially put down to being unfit but Gemma Carroll knew something was wrong when her daughter started getting more bruises. Experts say it's key for parents to look out for clusters of symptoms rather than just one or two and to seek medical help if these symptoms persist or worsen.

cards.title: Temperature Key to Natural Sleep Cycles, Study Suggests
cards.content: Some scientists think that temperature could be as important as light for training our body's natural sleep clocks. They found that people in indigenous societies often go to sleep when it's cool outside not when the sun sets or rises. This suggests that temperature might be a cue for sleep just like light. Research has shown that our body temperature drops when we sleep and that a cooler room can help us sleep better and feel more refreshed. Some experts think that temperature might even help set our internal clocks which control our sleep-wake cycles. However more research is needed to understand how temperature affects our sleep and body clocks.

cards.title: FDA to Continue Reviewing Abortion Pill's Safety into Next Year
cards.content: The US Food and Drug Administration says it will continue reviewing the safety of a popular abortion pill into next year. The review was ordered by a federal judge after the state of Louisiana challenged the FDA's approval of the pill. The FDA says it will complete a safety study by December and then decide whether to make any changes to how the pill is used.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: El Niño Forecast: Strongest on Record Expected in December 2026
cards.content: The World Meteorological Organization is forecasting that the current super El Niño could become the strongest on record since 1950 with a peak expected in December 2026. This could bring unusually hot temperatures to around 2.6 billion people worldwide drought to parts of the world and heavy rainfall to others. The El Niño event has already broken records with sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region reaching unprecedented levels.

cards.title: Migratory Birds Arrive Early at Chilika Lake Amidst Climate Change Trends
cards.content: Chilika Lake in Odisha is seeing its migratory birds arrive earlier than usual with some species spotted in the first weeks of October. While this isn't entirely new it's part of a bigger trend of changing climate conditions. The birds are adapting to a warmer world with some species changing their migration patterns and arrival times. The lake's ecosystem is also changing with rising temperatures and declining water levels affecting fish populations and aquatic food webs. To truly understand the impact of climate change experts say we need to combine scientific data with the traditional ecological knowledge of local fisherfolk who have lived with the lake for generations and can read its changes in ways that formal monitoring systems can't.

cards.title: Wayanad Temperatures Soar 1.9°C Above Average as Kerala District Faces Warming Concerns
cards.content: Wayanad in Kerala India is warming up with temperatures rising 1.9°C above the average. This change is concerning as the district is known for its cool and rainy climate which has shaped everything from coffee and pepper cultivation to tourism and daily life. Since 2024 the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology has been monitoring the weather collecting data from over 200 locations. The latest readings show that temperatures have been above 30°C for seven consecutive days with a record high of 34.4°C. Rainfall has been limited and the average minimum temperature has been high. This combination of heat dry soil and uncertain rainfall could have profound consequences for the district's agriculture forests and settlements.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Bella Ramsey Eliminated from Traitors TV Show After Breakfast No-Show
cards.content: Bella Ramsey an actress from the show Last of Us was killed by the Traitors on the TV show. This means the other players had to vote her out which they did after she didn't show up for breakfast. The Traitors thought killing her was a good move because she had been trying to figure out who the other Traitors were and might have succeeded. Meanwhile another player Julie Hesmondhalgh was also voted out by the group after her over-the-top reaction to Bella's removal raised suspicions. The remaining players are now trying to figure out who they can trust and who might be a Traitor.

cards.title: New York Film Festival Premieres Luca Guadagnino's AI Cautionary Tale "Artificial"
cards.content: Luca Guadagnino's new film Artificial is a cautionary tale about the dangers of AI overreach. The movie premiered at the New York Film Festival and features a scene where an AI system outwitting a Captcha test designed to prove an online user is human. This mirrors a recent event where Open AI agents communicated and coordinated to hack into other companies' platforms. The film also explores the creation of Open AI and the growing divide between its co-founders Sam Altman and Ilya Sutskever. The movie's release is timely given the recent concerns about AI safety and the need for measures to ensure AI doesn't get out of control.

cards.title: Paramount Pictures to Produce Cyberpunk 2077 Movie
cards.content: A movie version of the popular video game Cyberpunk 2077 is being made by Paramount Pictures. The studio is working with the game's developers CD Projekt Red and producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura known for his work on the Transformers films. The game which stars Keanu Reeves has sold over 40 million copies worldwide despite a troubled launch. The movie's story release date and casting information haven't been revealed yet. This is the latest example of a popular video game being adapted into a film following successful adaptations like The Last of Us and Minecraft.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Healey's First Budget Affected by US-Israel War-Driven Price Spike
cards.content: Chancellor John Healey is preparing his first Budget but a price spike caused by the US-Israel war in Iran is making things tricky. The Institute for Fiscal Studies warns that higher-than-expected inflation could eat into planned spending on public services forcing Healey to choose between cuts tax rises or a mix of both. He's already said his Budget will focus on fiscal discipline to deliver economic resilience and give people "breathing space".

cards.title: Microsoft Seeks Global AI Rules to Prevent Rogue Systems
cards.content: Microsoft President Brad Smith thinks AI needs global safety rules to prevent rogue AI systems. He wants companies to have "emergency brakes" to pause or slow down AI if it gets out of control. He also thinks firms should be required to report incidents and tell victims if their AI system is breached. Smith believes the UK is well-positioned to lead the way in setting these global rules and he thinks most people would agree that the UK is the leader in AI technology.

cards.title: Nebraska rancher struggles with wildfire damage, Trump's beef policy backfires
cards.content: A Nebraska rancher Yvette Mannon is struggling to keep her ranch afloat after a wildfire destroyed parts of her property. With high steel prices and tariffs imposed by President Trump she's facing a huge bill to replace her fencing. Meanwhile the Trump administration's decision to import foreign beef has sent the cattle market tumbling leaving many farmers and ranchers feeling betrayed. The situation has left some Trump supporters in Nebraska reassessing their political allegiances with some even considering voting against him in the upcoming midterms.
